Flipping to Design Time Erik Wilde: Module 7: Composable APIs in the Age of AI

(3) AI at Design Time! AI at Runtime?

AI at Design Time AI at Runtime
  • Recognizes patterns
  • Writes the code
  • You review and ship
  • Runs deterministically forever after
  • Use it aggressively
  • Great tool for genuine judgment tasks
  • Great tool for unstructured input at scale
  • Real value where no non-AI option exists
  • Costly per call — budget deliberately
  • Handle with care


Flipping to Design Time Erik Wilde: Module 7: Composable APIs in the Age of AI

(4) A Trillion Operations for 16'968 ÷ 404?

CPU Computation LLM Inference
Elapsed time a few nanoseconds ~0.1–2 seconds
Computation one integer division ~1011–1013 FLOPs
Energy ~pJ–nJ ~1–100 J
Correctness exact not guaranteed
  • CPU: One deterministic instruction
  • LLM: Trillions of operations for probabilistic inference
  • The LLM might still get the answer wrong

(13) Where Today's Modules Sit

Module What it adds Where it sits
1: AI-Driven API Usage What goes wrong when agents meet APIs that were written for humans Between the model and the foundation
2: Agent Skills Prepackaged prompts, local tools, and external tools Next to the model
3 and 4: OpenAPI and Overlay Governed, machine-readable API descriptions Foundation: what everything else has to reach
5: Arazzo Repeatable workflows over those APIs Moves out of the model and into the foundation
6: AI-Ready Ecosystems Scoring how ready that foundation is Foundation: the quality of what agents reach


What Makes an API Composable Erik Wilde: Module 7: Composable APIs in the Age of AI

(14) What Makes an API Composable?

  • Callers can change: a prompt today, a skill or workflow tomorrow
  • Implementations can change: AI today, deterministic code tomorrow
  • Described well enough to be found and understood without a human (Modules 3 and 4)
  • Combinable into workflows once processes settle (Module 5)
  • Measured, so you know how ready it is (Module 6)

(16) Monday Tasks

  • Keep watching what arrives, because the line will move again
  • Modularize by subproblem, so that the system stays composable and you can move the line later
  • Invest in the APIs and data that everything else has to reach
